title: 1970 AHSME Problem 33
statement: Find the sum of the digits of all the numerals in the sequence \(1,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) \(4,\) \(\ldots,\) \(10000.\)

solutions.text:
Write the integers from \(0\) through \(9999\) using four digits with leading zeros. In each of the four positions, every digit \(0,\) \(1,\) \(\ldots,\) \(9\) appears \(1000\) times. Thus their total digit sum is \[ \begin{gathered} 4\cdot1000(0+1+\cdots+9)\\ =4000\cdot45\\ =180000. \end{gathered} \] Replacing \(0\) by \(10000\) adds \(1,\) so the requested sum is \(180001.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
